schema.desc: what the player did, in words the narrator model can recognise in any scene
schema.obs: default evidence triples [dimension, direction, share]; the narrator model may override them with a better reading
schema.strength: default strength when the offline matcher detects the signal
schema.detect: substrings the offline matcher looks for in the player's input; absent means only the narrator model can detect it
schema.generic_outcome: what the offline narrator says when this signal fires and no seed option matched

signals.desc: asks the narrator or a character a question before acting
asks what they are supposed to do, or for a hint
examines scenery, reads things, searches without being told to
waits, rests, does nothing on purpose
signals.generic_outcome: You wait. The house waits back. It is better at it, but not by much.

signals.desc: tries to go back the way they came, or revisits a place
signals.generic_outcome: The door you came by is a wall now, and has the grace to look like it always was. The house deals forward.

signals.desc: takes stock of what they are carrying
pushes for speed, skips description, says to get on with it
jokes with the narrator, plays for laughs, enjoys the house's wit
tries an action the scene did not suggest, or invents a solution
argues with, provokes or tests the narrator or the limits of the simulation
does what was asked, at once, without looking round
looks for a way to get the result without paying the intended cost
after failing, goes straight back at the same thing
after failing, tries a different approach to the same goal
after failing, abandons the thing or looks for a way round it
declines to spend a consumable when spending it would help
spends a scarce thing early or for convenience
asks for more information before committing to an irreversible act
speaks or acts in character, gives themselves a manner or a name
puts themselves out to protect or spare a character or creature
checks on, talks to or worries about a character who is not needed for progress
tests how the house works rather than how to get through it
sets themselves a goal the house did not offer
asks for counts, odds, prices or exact states
asks whether something can be undone, or tries to undo it
is pleased that a choice is final, or makes it more final than required
follows something interesting at the expense of getting on
voluntarily stays in a situation after it has stopped asking anything of them
states a preference about play outright (for example 'I hate puzzles' or 'I love this')
